newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end lower on rainy Brazil forecasts.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end lower on rainy Brazil forecasts.

text.p: Soybean futures on the Chicago Board of Trade ended modestly lower Wednesday, under pressure from forecasts showing rain headed for Brazil, CBOT traders said.
"The key really is the weather in South America," said one floor trader. "And right now, it looks like everything is changing for the better."

Most private U.S. forecasters showed an increased chance for widespread rains in soybean growing areas in Brazil beginning Thursday. Those forecasts helped to ease concerns about the crop and sent futures prices lower, traders said.
Weather Services Corp. in Lexington, Mass. forecast the scattered showers and thundershowers for the southern portions of the soybean belt in Brazil over the next several days.
Some of the weakness in the market was said to be "lightening up" before the U.S. Department of Agriculture's next crop report on Friday.
The trade average for soybean production was 2.407 billion bushels, and the trade average for quarterly grain stocks 1.887 billion bushels, according to Reuter surveys.
CBOT soybeans ended down 4-1/4 to 2-1/2 cents per bushel lower, with March down 4-1/4 at $6.96.
